newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish Cypriots ease off-shore regulations.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriots ease off-shore regulations.

text.p: The Turkish Cypriot parliament adopted amendments to ease regulations on the operation of off-shore companies in northern Cyprus, Economy Minister Erdal Onurhan said on Tuesday.
"The aim is to provide grounds for off-shore companies to compete with the conditions in other countries," Onurhan told Reuters.
The amendments, approved by parliament on Monday, ban the disclosure of official records on off-shore companies. The records will only be available by a court order or authorisation by the minister.

The article, providing for a paid in capital of $5,000 for off-shore companies has also been changed in favour of the companies to require a committment for the capital, removing the need for it to be pre-paid.
The fees for the registration, capital increase and share transfers of the off-shore firms have also been cut by 50 percent, bringing them down to 0.4 percent from 0.8 percent.
The amendments also dropped the annual operation fees to $500 from $1,000 and the annual fixed income tax to $500 from $2,000.
The new arrangements will take effect after being published in the Official Gazette, Onurhan said.
There are 26 off-shore companies registered in the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, only recognised by Turkey.
